_meta.description: AI/LLM domain knowledge graph — NLP, Transformer, LLM, Agent, RAG, Embedding, Prompt Engineering, Fine-tuning

node_types.Domain: 顶层技术域，如 大语言模型
node_types.Tech: 核心技术栈，如 Transformer / RAG / Agent
node_types.Concept: 技术概念，需要候选人深度理解
node_types.Pitfall: 常见踩坑点、面试高频陷阱题

edge_types.HAS_COMPONENT: Tech 包含某个子组件或子概念
edge_types.LEADS_TO: 面试追问路径：A问完自然引出B，带 question_hint
edge_types.HAS_PITFALL: 该技术/概念有一个常见坑点
edge_types.REQUIRES: 理解A需要先掌握B（前置依赖）
edge_types.RELATED_TO: 两个节点强相关，面试中可横向延伸

nodes.label: NLP
nodes.description: 让计算机理解和生成人类语言的技术领域，是LLM的基础学科

nodes.label: Transformer
nodes.description: 基于自注意力的序列建模架构，彻底取代RNN，成为现代LLM的基础

nodes.label: LLM
nodes.description: 在海量文本上预训练的超大规模语言模型，如GPT/Qwen/LLaMA系列

nodes.label: Embedding
nodes.description: 将文本映射到稠密向量空间，是语义检索和RAG的基础

nodes.label: RAG
nodes.description: 通过外部知识检索增强LLM生成，减少幻觉，支持知识更新

nodes.label: Fine-tuning
nodes.description: 在预训练模型基础上用特定数据进一步训练，使模型适配下游任务

nodes.label: Prompt Engineering
nodes.description: 通过设计输入提示引导LLM产出高质量输出的工程方法

nodes.label: LLM Agent
nodes.description: 以LLM为决策核心，具备规划、记忆、工具调用能力的自主系统

nodes.label: Attention Mechanism
nodes.description: 通过Q/K/V矩阵计算序列元素两两相关性，复杂度O(n²)

nodes.label: Multi-Head Attention
nodes.description: 将Attention分到h个子空间并行计算再拼接，捕获不同粒度的语义

nodes.label: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
nodes.description: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V，除以√d_k防止梯度消失

nodes.label: Positional Encoding
nodes.description: 向embedding注入位置信息，原始Transformer用正弦余弦函数

nodes.label: RoPE
nodes.description: 通过旋转矩阵编码相对位置，支持外推到更长序列，LLaMA/Qwen采用

nodes.label: KV Cache
nodes.description: 缓存历史token的K/V矩阵避免重复计算，推理加速的核心机制

nodes.label: Feed-Forward Network
nodes.description: Transformer中每个位置独立的两层全连接，通常用SwiGLU激活

nodes.label: Layer Normalization
nodes.description: 对特征维度归一化，Pre-LN(前置)比Post-LN训练更稳定

nodes.label: 预训练 (Pre-training)
nodes.description: 在海量无标注文本上自监督训练，CLM(因果语言建模)是GPT路线的核心

nodes.label: RLHF
nodes.description: 通过人类偏好数据训练奖励模型，再用PPO优化LLM对齐人类价值观

nodes.label: Reward Model
nodes.description: RLHF的评分器，学习人类偏好判断哪个回答更好

nodes.label: SFT (指令微调)
nodes.description: 用高质量指令-回复对进行监督训练，让模型学会遵循用户指令

nodes.label: LoRA
nodes.description: 冻结原始权重，只训练低秩分解的增量矩阵ΔW=AB，大幅降低显存

nodes.label: QLoRA
nodes.description: 将基础模型量化为4-bit NF4格式后再做LoRA，消费级GPU可微调70B模型

nodes.label: 向量检索
nodes.description: 将文本embedding化后用近似最近邻(ANN)算法召回语义相似文档

nodes.label: HNSW
nodes.description: 主流ANN索引算法，通过多层图结构实现次线性时间的近似最近邻搜索

nodes.label: Chunking策略
nodes.description: 文档切割粒度直接影响检索精度：过大上下文冗余，过小语义不完整

nodes.label: Reranking (重排序)
nodes.description: 用精度更高的Cross-Encoder对初步召回结果重新打分排序，精排阶段

nodes.label: 混合检索 (Hybrid Search)
nodes.description: 结合BM25关键词检索和向量语义检索，互补提升召回率

nodes.label: ReAct
nodes.description: 交替生成推理轨迹(Thought)和执行动作(Action)，每步基于观察更新

nodes.label: Tool Calling
nodes.description: LLM输出结构化JSON指令触发外部工具，结果回传至上下文继续推理

nodes.label: Agent记忆机制
nodes.description: 短期:当前对话窗口；长期:外部存储(向量库/DB)，通过检索注入上下文

nodes.label: Chain of Thought
nodes.description: 引导LLM逐步推理而非直接输出答案，显著提升复杂推理准确率

nodes.label: Few-shot Learning
nodes.description: 在Prompt中提供少量示例让LLM学习任务模式，无需参数更新

nodes.label: System Prompt
nodes.description: 对话开始前注入的角色设定和约束指令，优先级高于用户输入

nodes.label: Word2Vec
nodes.description: 早期静态词向量，通过预测上下文学习语义，不能处理一词多义

nodes.label: Sentence Transformer
nodes.description: 基于BERT的句级别向量模型，通过对比学习优化语义相似度

nodes.label: 对比学习
nodes.description: 正例拉近、负例推远，是训练高质量Embedding模型的核心范式

nodes.label: Tokenization
nodes.description: 将原始文本切割为模型可处理的token单元，直接影响语言理解边界

nodes.label: BPE (字节对编码)
nodes.description: GPT系列采用的分词算法，迭代合并高频字符对，平衡词表大小与覆盖率

nodes.label: Attention O(n²)复杂度
nodes.description: Self-Attention时间和显存复杂度随序列长度平方增长，长文本时显存爆炸

nodes.label: 位置编码外推失效
nodes.description: 模型在超出训练长度的序列上性能骤降，绝对位置编码无法外推

nodes.label: LLM幻觉 (Hallucination)
nodes.description: LLM自信地生成与事实不符的内容，根源是统计语言模型缺乏事实锚定

nodes.label: Lost-in-the-Middle
nodes.description: LLM对长上下文中间段落的关注度显著低于首尾，影响RAG准确率

nodes.label: Prompt Injection
nodes.description: 恶意用户通过精心构造输入覆盖系统提示词，劫持模型行为的安全攻击

nodes.label: 灾难性遗忘
nodes.description: 全量微调特定任务数据时，模型大量遗忘预训练阶段的通用能力

nodes.label: 奖励黑客 (Reward Hacking)
nodes.description: 模型找到奖励模型的漏洞获得高分但实际输出无意义，RLHF的核心风险

nodes.label: KV Cache显存占用
nodes.description: 长序列推理时KV Cache显存随batch_size和序列长度线性增长，OOM风险

nodes.label: Agent无限循环
nodes.description: 工具调用失败时Agent可能陷入重试死循环，需要max_iterations硬限制

nodes.label: Embedding空间坍缩
nodes.description: 训练不充分时所有向量聚集在小区域，余弦相似度失去区分能力

nodes.label: Context Engineering
nodes.description: 对注入LLM上下文窗口的信息进行工程化管理：选择、压缩、排布与动态更新，使有限token发挥最大价值

nodes.label: 多智能体系统
nodes.description: 多个专用Agent分工协作完成复杂任务，包括Supervisor模式、流水线模式和对等协商模式

nodes.label: Agent开发框架
nodes.description: LangChain/LangGraph等框架，提供图状态机、工具集成、记忆管理等Agent工程化能力

nodes.label: LLM推理优化
nodes.description: vLLM/Ollama等高性能推理框架，通过PagedAttention、连续批处理等技术大幅提升吞吐和降低延迟

nodes.label: MCP（模型上下文协议）
nodes.description: Anthropic提出的标准化工具集成协议，统一LLM与外部工具/数据源的交互接口，类比USB-C

nodes.label: 任务规划与拆解
nodes.description: LLM将复杂目标分解为有依赖关系的子任务序列，是多智能体系统的核心调度能力

nodes.label: Agent反思纠错
nodes.description: Agent对自身输出进行批判性评估，检测错误并主动修正，形成'规划-执行-反思'闭环

nodes.label: DPO（直接偏好优化）
nodes.description: 将奖励模型隐式嵌入策略模型，绕过强化学习直接优化偏好对齐，比RLHF更稳定简洁

nodes.label: 模型量化
nodes.description: 将模型权重从FP32/BF16压缩为INT8/INT4，降低显存和推理延迟，代价是轻微精度损失

nodes.label: PagedAttention
nodes.description: vLLM提出的KV Cache显存管理技术，借鉴操作系统分页思想消除显存碎片，支持大并发

nodes.label: 连续批处理
nodes.description: 推理服务动态插入新请求而非等待整个batch完成，GPU利用率从30%提升到70%+

nodes.label: LLM可观测性
nodes.description: 对LLM调用链路进行trace/span级别追踪，记录每步输入输出、延迟、Token消耗，支持多维归因分析

nodes.label: 上下文窗口管理
nodes.description: 长对话中选择性保留关键信息：滑动窗口、摘要压缩、重要性评分等策略维持有效上下文

nodes.label: Function/Tool Schema设计
nodes.description: JSON Schema格式的工具描述，name/description/parameters质量直接决定LLM工具选择准确率

nodes.label: 图状态机
nodes.description: LangGraph的核心抽象，用节点(Node)和边(Edge)描述Agent控制流，支持条件路由和循环

nodes.label: 上下文窗口溢出
nodes.description: 长对话/多轮Agent超出context limit时历史消息被截断，导致Agent失忆或任务失败

nodes.label: Tool Schema歧义
nodes.description: 工具描述含糊或参数命名不清时LLM频繁误调用，是Agent工程中最常见的准确率瓶颈

nodes.label: 多智能体状态冲突
nodes.description: 多个Agent并发修改共享状态时产生竞争条件，或子Agent结论相互矛盾导致协调失败

nodes.label: 首Token延迟（TTFT）
nodes.description: Time-To-First-Token过高导致用户感知卡顿，根因可能是prefill计算量大或调度队列积压

nodes.label: Computer Science Core
nodes.description: Core CS topics: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and networking.

nodes.label: Backend Engineering
nodes.description: Backend language, framework, API, and service engineering topics.

nodes.label: Database and Cache
nodes.description: Database, cache, transaction, index, and query optimization topics.

nodes.label: Distributed Systems
nodes.description: Microservices, message queues, consistency, and system design topics.

nodes.label: DevOps and Cloud Native
nodes.description: Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD topics.

nodes.label: Frontend Engineering
nodes.description: JavaScript, browser runtime, React, and frontend engineering topics.

nodes.label: Security and Quality Engineering
nodes.description: Authentication, web security, testing, and observability topics.

nodes.label: Data Structures
nodes.description: Core ways to organize and access data, shared by coding interviews and engineering trade-offs.

nodes.label: Array and Linked List
nodes.description: Contiguous storage versus linked storage; access, insertion, deletion, and cache-locality trade-offs.

nodes.label: Stack and Queue
nodes.description: Restricted linear structures used in parsing, monotonic stacks, BFS, and scheduling.

nodes.label: Hash Table
nodes.description: Maps keys to buckets with a hash function; collision handling and resizing matter.

nodes.label: Tree and Graph
nodes.description: Models hierarchical and network relationships; common traversals include DFS, BFS, and topological sort.

nodes.label: Hash Collision Degradation
nodes.description: Poor hash distribution or adversarial input can degrade expected O(1) operations.

nodes.label: Algorithms
nodes.description: General problem-solving methods used to assess abstraction, complexity analysis, and edge handling.

nodes.label: Complexity Analysis
nodes.description: Asymptotic analysis of time and space growth as input size increases.

nodes.label: Sorting and Searching
nodes.description: Common foundations where invariants, boundaries, and stability are frequently tested.

nodes.label: Dynamic Programming
nodes.description: Solves overlapping subproblems by defining states and transition equations.

nodes.label: DFS/BFS and Backtracking
nodes.description: Search strategies for trees, graphs, and combinatorial spaces; pruning and visited state are key.

nodes.label: DP State Explosion
nodes.description: Too many state dimensions can make time or space unacceptable.

nodes.label: Operating Systems
nodes.description: Program execution, resource management, memory, IO, and concurrency foundations.

nodes.label: Process and Thread
nodes.description: Processes own resources; threads are scheduling units within a process.

nodes.label: Concurrency and Locking
nodes.description: Protects shared state with synchronization primitives; races and visibility matter.

nodes.label: Virtual Memory
nodes.description: Address translation provides isolation and expansion through pages and page tables.

nodes.label: IO Multiplexing
nodes.description: Lets one thread manage many connections efficiently; select/poll/epoll differences are common.

nodes.label: Deadlock
nodes.description: Threads can wait on each other forever when deadlock conditions hold.

nodes.label: Computer Networks
nodes.description: Communication protocols, reliability, latency, and troubleshooting foundations.

nodes.label: TCP and UDP
nodes.description: TCP provides reliable byte streams; UDP provides low-overhead datagrams.

nodes.label: HTTP and HTTPS
nodes.description: HTTP defines request-response semantics; HTTPS adds encryption, authentication, and integrity.

nodes.label: DNS and CDN
nodes.description: DNS maps names to addresses; CDN improves latency and availability via edge nodes.

nodes.label: WebSocket and Long Connection
nodes.description: Provides bidirectional communication over one TCP connection for realtime use cases.

nodes.label: Head-of-Line Blocking
nodes.description: Earlier data can block later data delivery in TCP or multiplexed protocols.

nodes.label: Java
nodes.description: Mainstream backend language often paired with Spring, JVM, concurrency, and collections.

nodes.label: JVM Memory Model
nodes.description: Runtime memory areas, object allocation, and visibility semantics.

nodes.label: Java GC
nodes.description: Automatic memory management based on reachability, generations, and pause trade-offs.

nodes.label: Java Collections
nodes.description: Core containers with important implementation and thread-safety differences.

nodes.label: Java Thread Pool
nodes.description: Reuses threads and controls concurrency through core size, queue, max size, and rejection policy.

nodes.label: Thread Pool Queue Buildup
nodes.description: Unbounded queues or bad parameters can create memory growth and latency collapse.

nodes.label: Spring Boot
nodes.description: Common Java backend framework around dependency injection, web handling, transactions, and ecosystem integration.

nodes.label: IoC Container
nodes.description: Creates and wires beans to reduce manual object assembly and coupling.

nodes.label: AOP
nodes.description: Separates cross-cutting concerns such as logging, transactions, and authorization.

nodes.label: Spring MVC Request Flow
nodes.description: DispatcherServlet routes requests through mapping, binding, controller execution, and response handling.

nodes.label: Spring Transaction
nodes.description: Declarative transactions manage commit and rollback through proxies.

nodes.label: @Transactional Not Effective
nodes.description: Self-invocation, wrong visibility, or swallowed exceptions can bypass transaction proxies.

nodes.label: Python
nodes.description: Common scripting, backend, and AI engineering language.

nodes.label: GIL
nodes.description: CPython lock protecting interpreter state; affects CPU-bound multithreading.

nodes.label: asyncio and Coroutine
nodes.description: Event-loop concurrency for IO-heavy workloads.

nodes.label: Python Web Frameworks
nodes.description: Framework choices differ in typing, batteries-included features, and minimalism.

nodes.label: Python Packaging
nodes.description: Dependency isolation and version pinning affect reproducible deployment.

nodes.label: Blocking Call in Async Code
nodes.description: Blocking IO or CPU work in async paths can stall the event loop.

nodes.label: API Design
nodes.description: External service contract design affecting usability, evolution, performance, and security.

nodes.label: RESTful API
nodes.description: Uses resources, methods, and status codes to express interface semantics.

nodes.label: API Idempotency
nodes.description: Repeated requests should produce the same business result in retry-sensitive flows.

nodes.label: Rate Limiting and Degradation
nodes.description: Protects services from overload using token bucket, leaky bucket, or related patterns.

nodes.label: Pagination and Versioning
nodes.description: List APIs need cursor or offset pagination and compatibility strategy.

nodes.label: Backward-Incompatible API Change
nodes.description: Changing fields or status semantics can break old clients.

nodes.label: MySQL
nodes.description: Relational database topic centered on indexes, transactions, locks, plans, and storage engines.

nodes.label: MySQL Index
nodes.description: InnoDB commonly uses B+Tree indexes; compound indexes involve leftmost-prefix and covering rules.

nodes.label: Transaction and Isolation
nodes.description: Transactions provide ACID; isolation balances consistency and concurrency.

nodes.label: MySQL Locking
nodes.description: InnoDB uses row, gap, and next-key locks for concurrent updates and phantom prevention.

nodes.label: Execution Plan
nodes.description: EXPLAIN reveals access type, chosen index, estimated rows, and extra operations.

nodes.label: Index Miss
nodes.description: Functions on columns, implicit conversion, or leading wildcard LIKE can prevent index use.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.description: In-memory data structure service for cache, counters, rate limits, leaderboards, and locks.

nodes.label: Redis Data Structures
nodes.description: Different structures imply different complexity and memory trade-offs.

nodes.label: Cache Patterns
nodes.description: Common approaches include Cache Aside, Read Through, and Write Through.

nodes.label: Redis Persistence
nodes.description: RDB and AOF trade recovery speed, data-loss window, and write amplification.

nodes.label: Redis Distributed Lock
nodes.description: SET NX EX based locks must handle expiry, renewal, and safe release.

nodes.label: Cache Penetration/Breakdown/Avalanche
nodes.description: Cache misses or mass expiry can push traffic into the database.

nodes.label: Message Queue
nodes.description: Asynchronous messaging for decoupling, buffering, and traffic smoothing.

nodes.label: Delivery Semantics
nodes.description: Messaging systems trade reliability and performance; business idempotency is often required.

nodes.label: Message Ordering
nodes.description: Ordering usually depends on routing the same key to the same partition or queue.

nodes.label: Retry and Dead Letter Queue
nodes.description: Failures need retry, backoff, and isolation to avoid blocking the main flow.

nodes.label: Kafka Partition and Consumer Group
nodes.description: Kafka scales throughput with partitions; a partition is consumed by only one consumer in a group.

nodes.label: Duplicate Message Consumption
nodes.description: Retries and offset timing can cause duplicate delivery; consumers need idempotency.

nodes.label: Microservices
nodes.description: Splits systems into independently deployable services with governance and failure isolation.

nodes.label: Service Discovery
nodes.description: Callers discover dynamic service instances through a registry.

nodes.label: RPC and HTTP Call
nodes.description: Service calls require serialization, timeout, retry, and connection-pool design.

nodes.label: Circuit Breaker and Fallback
nodes.description: Fails fast or returns fallback when downstream services are unstable.

nodes.label: Distributed Tracing
nodes.description: Connects cross-service request paths to locate errors and latency.

nodes.label: Retry Storm
nodes.description: Unbounded retries amplify downstream failures without timeout, backoff, limits, and breakers.

nodes.label: System Design
nodes.description: Designs complete systems from requirements, capacity, data model, APIs, scalability, and recovery.

nodes.label: Capacity Estimation
nodes.description: Estimates DAU, QPS, data volume, bandwidth, and bottlenecks.

nodes.label: Load Balancing
nodes.description: Distributes traffic across instances with health checks and routing algorithms.

nodes.label: Sharding and Replication
nodes.description: Improves capacity and availability while adding consistency and routing complexity.

nodes.label: Consistency and Availability
nodes.description: Distributed systems choose trade-offs between strong consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

nodes.label: Hot Key / Hot Partition
nodes.description: Skewed traffic can overload one key, shard, or partition.

nodes.label: Linux
nodes.description: Base environment for deployment and troubleshooting.

nodes.label: Process and Resource Tools
nodes.description: Observes processes, CPU, memory, and file handles.

nodes.label: Network Troubleshooting Tools
nodes.description: Diagnoses ports, connectivity, and protocol behavior.

nodes.label: File Permission
nodes.description: Linux permissions affect read, write, execute, and deployment security.

nodes.label: Shell Scripting
nodes.description: Automates operations and data processing with pipes and command composition.

nodes.label: Permission and Path Issue
nodes.description: Deployment failures often come from permissions, users, working directory, or environment variables.

nodes.label: Docker
nodes.description: Containerized delivery with consistent runtime and lightweight isolation.

nodes.label: Image and Layer
nodes.description: Image layers and Dockerfile order affect cache reuse and image size.

nodes.label: Container Network
nodes.description: Containers communicate through bridge, host, or custom networks.

nodes.label: Docker Volume
nodes.description: Volumes and bind mounts persist data and mount configuration.

nodes.label: Docker Compose
nodes.description: Compose orchestrates local multi-container environments through YAML.

nodes.label: Large Docker Image
nodes.description: Uncleaned dependencies and build artifacts make images slow and risky to deploy.

nodes.label: Kubernetes
nodes.description: Cloud-native orchestration for deployment, scheduling, service discovery, autoscaling, and self-healing.

nodes.label: Pod and Deployment
nodes.description: Pod is the smallest scheduling unit; Deployment manages replicas and rolling updates.

nodes.label: Service and Ingress
nodes.description: Service provides stable access; Ingress handles layer-7 routing.

nodes.label: ConfigMap and Secret
nodes.description: Configuration and secrets should be separated from images.

nodes.label: HPA and Health Check
nodes.description: HPA scales workload; probes control restart and traffic readiness.

nodes.label: Probe Misconfiguration
nodes.description: Bad probe path, timeout, or delay can cause restarts or premature traffic.

nodes.label: JavaScript / TypeScript
nodes.description: Frontend foundation language topics around typing, closures, prototypes, async, and modules.

nodes.label: Closure and Scope
nodes.description: Closures retain access to lexical environment.

nodes.label: Prototype and this
nodes.description: Prototype chain controls property lookup; this depends on call form.

nodes.label: Event Loop
nodes.description: Schedules macro tasks and microtasks in async execution.

nodes.label: TypeScript Type System
nodes.description: Static types improve maintainability through generics, unions, and structural typing.

nodes.label: Async Execution Order Mistake
nodes.description: Misunderstanding microtask priority leads to wrong execution-order reasoning.

nodes.label: Component and State
nodes.description: Components describe UI; props flow down and state drives re-rendering.

nodes.label: Hooks
nodes.description: Hooks give function components state, effects, and memoization.

nodes.label: Render and Reconciliation
nodes.description: React computes UI updates through virtual DOM and reconciliation.

nodes.label: Frontend State Management
nodes.description: Separates local state, server state, and global state.

nodes.label: useEffect Infinite Loop
nodes.description: Wrong dependencies or state updates inside effects can cause repeated rendering.

nodes.label: Browser Runtime
nodes.description: Runtime environment for frontend code, covering rendering, networking, isolation, and performance.

nodes.label: Browser Render Pipeline
nodes.description: Builds DOM/CSSOM and runs layout, paint, and compositing.

nodes.label: Browser Cache
nodes.description: HTTP caching reduces network requests through Cache-Control, ETag, and related headers.

nodes.label: Same-Origin Policy and CORS
nodes.description: Same-origin policy restricts cross-site access; CORS authorizes selected requests.

nodes.label: Frontend Performance
nodes.description: Optimizes loading, interaction, and visual stability.

nodes.label: CORS Credentials Misconfiguration
nodes.description: Credentialed cross-origin requests cannot use wildcard origin.

nodes.label: Web Security
nodes.description: Common web attacks and defenses around input, authorization, session, and outbound access.

nodes.label: SQL Injection
nodes.description: Attackers inject SQL; parameterized queries and least privilege are basic defenses.

nodes.label: XSS
nodes.description: Malicious scripts run in pages; escaping, CSP, and output handling matter.

nodes.label: CSRF
nodes.description: Uses a user login session to trigger unintended requests; SameSite and CSRF tokens help.

nodes.label: SSRF
nodes.description: Tricks servers into accessing internal or sensitive addresses; whitelist and network isolation help.

nodes.label: Trusting User Input
nodes.description: Treating user input as trusted amplifies injection, authorization, and business bypass risks.

nodes.label: Authentication and Authorization
nodes.description: Authentication identifies users; authorization decides what they can do.

nodes.label: Session and Cookie
nodes.description: Server-side sessions associate user state with cookies.

nodes.label: JWT
nodes.description: Self-contained tokens suit stateless auth but complicate revocation and leakage response.

nodes.label: OAuth2
nodes.description: Third-party authorization; authorization-code flow with PKCE is safer.

nodes.label: RBAC/ABAC
nodes.description: RBAC uses roles; ABAC uses attributes and policy for finer-grained control.

nodes.label: Broken Access Control
nodes.description: Checking only login or hiding buttons on frontend can allow horizontal or vertical privilege bypass.

nodes.label: Testing
nodes.description: Automated verification that reduces regression risk.

nodes.label: Unit Testing
nodes.description: Isolates small units and checks outputs, boundaries, and exception paths.

nodes.label: Integration Testing
nodes.description: Verifies cooperation among modules, database, or external services.

nodes.label: Mock and Stub
nodes.description: Test doubles isolate dependencies; over-mocking lowers realism.

nodes.label: Load Testing
nodes.description: Simulates traffic to observe throughput, latency, error rate, and bottlenecks.

nodes.label: Flaky Test
nodes.description: Tests relying on time, order, external services, or shared state can fail intermittently.

nodes.label: Observability Engineering
nodes.description: Logs, metrics, and tracing used to understand running systems and troubleshoot incidents.

nodes.label: Logging
nodes.description: Records business events and error context; structure and sensitive data matter.

nodes.label: Metrics Monitoring
nodes.description: Observes throughput, latency, error rate, and resource utilization.

nodes.label: Tracing
nodes.description: Captures cross-service request paths and durations.

nodes.label: Alerting and SLO
nodes.description: Alerts should track user impact and SLOs, not noisy low-value symptoms.

nodes.label: Alert Fatigue
nodes.description: Too many low-quality alerts make teams ignore real incidents.

nodes.label: React
nodes.description: Mainstream frontend UI framework around components, state, rendering, and Hooks.

edges.question_hint: NLP领域经历了从RNN到Transformer的范式转变，你能讲讲Transformer解决了RNN的哪些根本问题吗？
Transformer的核心是Attention，你能从数学角度解释Q/K/V的含义，以及为什么要除以√d_k吗？
多头注意力(MHA)相比单头有什么优势？每个head学到的是同样的东西吗？
MHA的复杂度是O(n²)，在长文本场景下显存会爆炸，你了解哪些优化方案？比如FlashAttention或GQA？
原始的正弦位置编码有长度外推的限制，现在LLaMA/Qwen用的是RoPE，它解决了什么问题？
KV Cache是推理加速的关键，但batch_size一大显存就不够，你们是怎么处理这个问题的？了解PagedAttention吗？
LLM的能力来自预训练，CLM(因果语言建模)的训练目标是什么？为什么Next Token Prediction能让模型涌现出推理能力？
预训练完成后模型并不会对话，SFT是怎么让它学会遵循指令的？数据质量和数量哪个更重要？
SFT之后还有RLHF，为什么SFT不够？RLHF的PPO训练过程你能讲一下吗？
奖励模型是RLHF的核心，但它本身也可能被模型'欺骗'——你了解Reward Hacking是怎么发生的吗？
GPT系列用BPE分词，你了解BPE的构建过程吗？中文和英文在tokenize时有什么本质差异？
早期的词向量用Word2Vec，它和现在基于Transformer的Embedding有什么本质区别？一词多义问题是怎么解决的？
Word2Vec是词级别的，RAG需要句子级别的向量，Sentence Transformer是怎么训练的？
对比学习训练Embedding时有个常见问题叫向量空间坍缩，你遇到过吗？是怎么检测和避免的？
RAG的召回阶段你用的是什么检索方式？纯向量检索有什么局限性？
纯向量检索对关键词精确匹配效果差，你们有没有引入混合检索？BM25和向量怎么融合分数？
混合检索之后召回了很多候选，精排阶段你用的是什么Reranker？Cross-Encoder和Bi-Encoder的区别是什么？
Reranker的效果很依赖初始召回的chunk质量，你们的chunk策略是固定大小还是语义切分？
即使检索到了相关chunk，塞进上下文还有个Lost-in-the-Middle问题，你了解吗？是怎么缓解的？
全量微调显存压力很大，你们用的是LoRA还是全参数微调？LoRA的rank怎么选的，有什么依据？
LoRA还需要全精度加载基础模型，QLoRA在这基础上做了什么优化？NF4量化的原理是什么？
LoRA/QLoRA能一定程度缓解灾难性遗忘，你们在微调后有没有做通用能力的评估？具体怎么测的？
你在项目里怎么设计Prompt的？Few-shot示例的选取有什么讲究？动态few-shot和静态few-shot有什么区别？
Few-shot之外，CoT(思维链)也是常用技巧，你了解为什么让模型'think step by step'能提升准确率吗？
CoT通常通过System Prompt引导，你们的System Prompt是怎么设计和迭代的？有没有做Prompt版本管理？
System Prompt设计不当会有Prompt Injection的风险，你们有没有做防御？常见的攻击手法是什么？
你们的Agent是怎么做任务规划的？用的是ReAct模式吗？Thought/Action/Observation分别负责什么？
ReAct的Action阶段依赖Tool Calling，LLM是怎么知道要调用哪个工具的？工具描述(schema)怎么设计？
多轮对话中Agent需要记住之前的操作，你们是怎么管理上下文的？短期记忆和长期记忆怎么区分？
如果工具调用一直失败，Agent会怎么处理？你们有没有遇到过Agent陷入死循环的问题？怎么检测和中断？
Context Engineering和Prompt Engineering有什么区别？当对话轮次很多、上下文快撑满时，你们是怎么决定保留哪些信息、丢弃哪些的？
上下文压缩有哪些常见策略？摘要压缩和滑动窗口各有什么适用场景？怎么评估压缩后信息损失？
在多智能体系统里，Supervisor怎么把任务拆解分配给子Agent？任务之间有依赖关系时是怎么处理的？
子Agent执行完后怎么判断结果是否符合预期？你们的反思纠错机制是怎么设计的？最多允许几轮反思？
多个Agent各自反思后给出了相互矛盾的结论，你们是怎么做最终裁决的？有没有遇到这种冲突情况？
LangGraph用图状态机描述Agent控制流，你们是怎么设计节点和边的？条件路由是怎么实现的？遇到过环路（cycle）的问题吗？
图状态机运行时每个节点的输入输出怎么追踪？你们用LangSmith还是自己搭的追踪方案？遇到Agent行为异常时怎么定位？
可观测性数据里你们关注哪些指标？怎么通过trace数据发现Agent在某个节点反复循环的问题？
vLLM的核心创新是PagedAttention，你能解释一下它怎么解决KV Cache的显存碎片问题的？和传统静态分配相比有什么优势？
PagedAttention解决了显存问题，但GPU利用率还是低，连续批处理是怎么提升吞吐的？iteration-level scheduling是什么意思？
连续批处理提高了吞吐，但可能加剧单个请求的TTFT延迟，你们是怎么在吞吐和延迟之间做权衡的？有没有做SLA保障？
你提到了KV Cache，vLLM的PagedAttention就是为了更好地管理KV Cache显存，你了解它的分页原理吗？
RLHF需要单独训练奖励模型，流程很复杂，DPO是怎么绕过这一步的？它的核心数学思想是什么？在实践中DPO有什么局限性？
工具调用现在有了更标准化的协议MCP，你了解它吗？MCP和直接写Function Schema有什么区别？它解决了什么工程痛点？
你们在设计工具Schema时有没有遇到LLM经常调用错工具或者参数填错的问题？description怎么写才能减少歧义？
单个Agent能力有限，你们有没有做多智能体系统？是Supervisor-Worker模式还是对等协商？怎么处理子Agent失败的情况？
Prompt Engineering是优化单次输入，Context Engineering是管理整个上下文窗口，你在工程实践中怎么区分这两个层次的优化？
